A PROCESS RECORD, NOT A DETECTOR

Record in-class drafting without surveillance

For writing teachers who need useful evidence of student choices during class.

Try it with sample data
See three completed tickets.
Start a class session
Students use class nicknames.
Sessions expire automatically.
Free for classes up to 40.
Four checkpoints make the drafting process easier to discuss.

LIVE PREVIEW

A ticket stays short

Students name one claim, one evidence location, one revision, and one next step.

03 / Quiet Maple

Claim
Memory acts like a second setting.

Revision
I moved the scene before my explanation.

THREE STOPS, ONE CLASS PERIOD

How it works
1
Create a session

Add the class name, prompt, and deletion date. Keep the private teacher link.

2
Share the code

Students use a class nickname and answer four short prompts.

3
Review the choices

Read each ticket beside the draft. Export the full session as CSV.

CLEAR BOUNDARIES

What this does not do
No AI detection
No webcam or microphone
No keystroke logging
No claim of proving authorship

The ticket gives teachers a starting point for feedback. It does not judge who wrote a draft.
